title: Artin approximation by an etale local algebra
statement: Let A be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let p be a prime ideal of A [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and let f_1, ..., f_m be polynomials in A[x_1, ..., x_n]. Suppose that (a_1, ..., a_n) is a solution of all f_j=0 in the maximal-ideal completion of A_p [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. If A_p is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], then for every integer N>=1 there exist an etale ring map A to A', a prime ideal p' of A' lying over p, and a solution (b_1, ..., b_n) in A' of all f_j=0 such that the residue-field map kappa(p) to kappa(p') is an isomorphism and a_i-b_i belongs to (p')^N times the maximal-ideal completion of A'_{p'} for every i.

source.place: Tag 0CAR, lemma-approximation-property-variant (Smoothing Ring Maps, Section 07XA), statement and proof.

proof.text: Put $R=A_{\mathfrak p}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pR$, and $H=\widehat R$. Localization preserves Noetherianity, and completion preserves Noetherianity, so both $R$ and $H$ are Noetherian. The G-ring hypothesis and the completion-regularity theorem make $R\to H$ regular. Popescu therefore presents $H$ as a colimit of a small filtered diagram of smooth $R$-algebras $B_j$, with $R$-algebra coprojections.

Regard each $f_j$ as a polynomial over $R$ and set $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$. Evaluation at the given tuple defines an $R$-algebra map $v:P\to H$, since every relation evaluates to zero. The finite-presentation factorization theorem supplies a stage $B$ and maps $P\xrightarrow{u}B\xrightarrow{w}H$ with $wu=v$. Thus, for $z_i=u(x_i)$, one has $f_j(z)=0$ in $B$ and $w(z_i)=a_i$. The affine morphism $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is smooth by the conclusion of the Popescu presentation in step 1.

source.place: Proof of Tag 07QZ, smooth factorization; Tags 00QO (lemma-characterize-finite-presentation) and 07C3 (lemma-when-colimit)

proof.text: Fix $N\geq1$. Apply [lem-trf-smooth-formal-point-etale-approximation] to the Noetherian local ring $R$, the smooth $R$-algebra $B$, and $w$. It gives $E,t,\mathfrak q=\mathfrak mE$, with trivial residue-field extension, and $T=E_{\mathfrak q}$ with $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mT$. Set $c_i=t(z_i)$. Since $t$ is an $R$-algebra map, evaluation of every $f_j$ at $c$ is $t(f_j(z))=0$. The lemma applied to $z_i$ gives $\widehat\lambda(a_i)-\iota_T(c_i/1)\in\mathfrak n^N\widehat T$.

source.place: Tag 07QZ, smooth-section lifting in its proof; precision-N refinement recorded in the cited node.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-pointed-etale-polynomial-solution-globalization] to $A,\mathfrak p,E,\mathfrak q,f,c$. Its hypotheses hold since $\mathfrak q$ lies over $\mathfrak m$. Obtain an etale $A$-algebra $A'$, its solution $b$, a prime $\mathfrak p'$ over $\mathfrak p$, and an $R$-algebra isomorphism $\theta:A'_{\mathfrak p'}\to T$ carrying $b_i/1$ to $c_i/1$. Write $S=A'_{\mathfrak p'}$ and $\mathfrak l=\mathfrak p'S$. Since $\mathfrak p'\cap A=\mathfrak p$, elements of $A\setminus\mathfrak p$ are units in $S$, giving its $R$-structure. If $\rho:\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ is the structural map, the residue isomorphism $\bar\theta$ satisfies $\bar\theta\rho$ equal to the isomorphism of step 3; hence $\rho$ is invertible. Since $\theta(\mathfrak l)=\mathfrak n$, the maps $S/\mathfrak l^r\to T/\mathfrak n^r$, $[s]\mapsto[\theta(s)]$, have inverses induced by $\theta^{-1}$ and commute with reduction and $R$. Applied coordinatewise to compatible sequences, they give inverse completion maps [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Writing $\widehat\mu:\widehat R\to\widehat S$ for the structural map, coordinatewise $\widehat\theta\widehat\mu=\widehat\lambda$. Also $\widehat\theta$ carries $b_i$ to $c_i$ and carries $(\mathfrak p')^N\widehat{A'_{\mathfrak p'}}$ onto $\mathfrak n^N\widehat T$: apply $\theta$ and $\theta^{-1}$ to the generators and finite sums defining these ideals. Applying its inverse to the preceding congruence gives $a_i-b_i\in(\mathfrak p')^N\widehat{A'_{\mathfrak p'}}$. This is the required congruence for the induced local completion map.
